gemini.rationale: The transaction transferred the Target Assets (T4) into the acquirer's legal vehicle, but the operational processes (T5) did not transfer; instead, they were accessed via a Services Agreement with EVOC, creating a gap_45. Furthermore, the management team (T6) was newly constituted (Chazen/Stavros) and did not include the EVOC employees running the day-to-day operations, creating a gap_56. Both gaps were mitigated at closing by the Services Agreement.

grok.rationale: gap_45=1 because the Target Assets (Karnes, Giddings, Ironwood interest) crossed into Pace LLC/Magnolia as the owned production base while day-to-day operating processes did not transfer and instead remained with EVOC under the concurrent Services Agreement; the proxy states TPGE 'will not be involved in the day-to-day operations of the Target Assets.' gap_56=0 because those processes and the ~100 dedicated EVOC field/technical employees stayed together at the seller affiliate under the same Services Agreement rather than processes moving without their operators; none of the EVOC personnel became company executive officers, and the new Chazen/Stavros management team was externally constituted. The Services Agreement (fixed fee, ~5-year term, transition-services tail) contractually absorbed the product-process separation at closing.

openai.rationale: The Target Assets crossed into Pace LLC, while day-to-day field, administrative, and back-office processes remained with EVOC and were supplied under a fixed-term Services Agreement, documenting a product-versus-process gap at closing. That gap was contractually absorbed because the Services Agreement required EVOC to provide services identical to those historically used to operate the assets. No separate process-versus-organization gap is documented: EVOC supplied both the operating processes and approximately 100 dedicated operating, technical, and field-level employees under the same agreement and under the Company's management direction.
